paragraphs: The X5 xDrive40e was BMW's first plug-in hybrid X5, produced from 2015 to 2018 as part of the F15 generation. It combines the B48 — a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine — with an electric motor integrated into the transmission. The powertrain delivers a combined output of 313hp, with an electric-only range of around 31km (19 miles) on the WLTP cycle. The xDrive40e was replaced by the xDrive50e in the later G05 generation with a significantly updated hybrid system and a larger battery offering up to 38 miles of electric range.
about.boldParagraph: The X5 xDrive40e is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

compatibility.intro: Because the xDrive40e combines a combustion engine with an electric motor, compatibility is more complex than a conventional engine replacement. The B48 engine in the xDrive40e is paired with a specific hybrid transmission and battery system — the engine cannot simply be swapped with a B48 from a non-hybrid BMW without significant electrical and software work.
